messages:
jess: FYI acme POC just reported repeated 502/503s during a live demo, they're paused and asking for an ETA. they were on the hosted sandbox model with ~20 concurrent streams.
sam: ugh. got the alert too. can someone grab the request IDs so we can trace? any deploys in the last 10m?
miguel: no deploys from runtime. i'm seeing a spike in request queue depth on the swarm for region-us-west. metrics: cpu 78%, gpu mem 92%, queue_len ~240, error_rate 12% in last 5m.
jay: ops-bot posted an autoscaler event at 1791122270: "scale_up delayed: insufficient idle GPUs detected, queued requests rerouted to fallback pool". that fallback pool is running smaller instances with lower concurrency.
jess: customer says the UI shows “service temporarily unavailable (502)”. they captured a request id: req_0a7f2c. sending it over.
miguel: traced req_0a7f2c -> node-83 fallback. logs show repeated timeouts to model-worker: "UpstreamError: call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (attempts=3)". also saw backend rate-limit marker: "throttle: capacity_exceeded".
sam: sounds like primary pool saturated and fallback overloaded. is our prefix cache causing hot-paths? any unusual prompt patterns from the POC? jess do you have examples?
jess: they were doing long streaming transcripts, many ~12k token requests. demo uses standard prompt + long user transcript.
amy: customer is also asking about dedicated capacity pricing and SOC2 evidence — want to keep them from churning while we triage.
miguel: long contexts + streaming = heavy KV cache usage, and that plus concurrent streams likely filled KV cache memory forcing eviction thrash. eviction thrash can blow up latency and cause upstream timeouts.
jay: short mitigation: switch their POC model to a shorter-context variant or turn on aggressive kv_cache eviction policy for that team. can do via the console or API.
sam: temporary config we can push: { model: "rwf-1-small", max_tokens: 4096, stream_chunk_ms: 200 } — reduces per-request mem. also enable prefix_cache=true for repeated instructions.
jess: can you push that now? customer wants any fix in the next 10m or they'll restart the demo.
miguel: pushing model swap for team acme-poc now.
ops-bot: deployment triggered by sam for acme-poc: apply config -> model=rwf-1-small, max_tokens=4096 at 1791122384. rollout 100% to sandbox.
jess: they confirmed switching models, but still seeing occasional 502s (less frequent). demo resumed.
sam: follow-up: we should also consider reserving a small dedicated pool for the POC to avoid noisy-neighbor. pricing note: reserved mini pool (2 x T4 equiv) add-on estimate ~$6k/mo — @jess please confirm with sales ops.
amy: security note: acme asked about VPC peering + customer-managed KMS for PII in transcripts. flagged for private deployment discussion. need to collect SOC2 docs before next POC meeting.
jess: I'll send the questionnaire template and ask them to sign the NDA so we can share SOC2 report.
miguel: longer-term: we need smarter autoscaler thresholds for short-burst demos — current scale up lag is ~90s due to job placement and image startup. propose warm standby pools for trial accounts.
jay: agree. also add a fallback queue size limit so we proactively reject instead of thundering when fallback overflow happens. that avoids cascading 5xx.
sam: opened ticket INF-4983 to track autoscaler warm standby + fallback hard limits. assigning to eng-runtime.
jess: customer is asking whether this would be covered in enterprise trial or needs dedicated. for the deal, they want guaranteed demo reliability — can we offer a short-term dedicated buffer for the demo window?
jay: yes, we can carve a burst reservation for the demo window (1-2h). ops can spin it up and bill as burst credits.
miguel: final note — we captured additional request IDs: req_0a7f2c, req_0a7f4d, req_0a7f9a. logs attached in the ticket INF-4982. if anyone needs them pull from S3: s3://redwood-logs/poc/acme/17911223/.
jess: acme said they want a postmortem and confirmation of fixes before next exec call. i'll own customer comms. thanks all :thumbsup:
sam: thanks team. I'll follow up on INF-4983 and schedule a short incident review tomorrow. miguel — can you draft the quick mitigation steps for runbook?
miguel: yes, will add a short runbook: swap to small model, lower max_tokens, enable prefix caching, temporary reserved burst, watch queue_len < 50.
ops-bot: alert cleared at 1791122640: error_rate returned to baseline."
